result.text: Title: Blizzard Online Character Generator Blizzard creates a cool online tool for creating characters for their new WoW expansion.
When creating a World of Warcraft character, you can start doing two things: While you are setting up your account, you can already come up with good character names.
The setup of your account starts with checking whether you have a battle.net account.
If you do not have one yet, you enter the account information and click the link you receive in the confirmation mail.
As soon as you have a battle.net account, you can check if you have an active WoW subscription.
If not, you can select the payment method.
If you choose credit card, enter your credit card information.
If you choose your bank account, enter your IBAN and BIC numbers.
After that you can log into the game and select realm, race and class of your character.
Until now, you should have come up with some good names.
You enter them one by one until a name is still available.
You get a confirmation, and some selfies of your character, as soon as a expansion is released you get another message.

You get a confirmation, and some selfies of your character, as soon as a expansion is released you get another message.

result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Sequence flows may cross lanes in one process. Use message flows across participant pools, never between lanes.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.
Use an event-based gateway when the first occurring event selects the path. Target supported catching events or receive tasks, not ordinary tasks.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
An ordinary embedded subprocess participates in normal sequence flow and may contain its own starts, ends, activities, gateways and flows.

result.rule: When the description states that work proceeds concurrently and that a later step must wait until all of that work is complete: Model the concurrent work as parallel branches and synchronize them with a parallel gateway before the dependent step.

When the description names multiple required activities in a phase, gives no order among them, and states that a later outcome occurs only after the phase is finished: Model each activity separately, use a parallel split for the unordered activities, and join their branches before modeling the later outcome.

When the description states that one activity is required while an independent activity is performed only when a condition holds.: Model an inclusive split so the required activity and the conditionally applicable activity can proceed, then use an inclusive join before their shared continuation.

When the description says that one of several alternatives is selected, or that an activity may occur: Model the choice or optional activity with an appropriate gateway, and reconnect the resulting paths before subsequent common work.
